title: Why Athaliah Tried to Destroy the Royal Line Completely
paragraphs: Why Athaliah Tried to Destroy the Royal Line Completely
There are demons that do not merely want to wound a generation.
They want to erase it.
Not weaken it. Not distract it. Not discourage it.
Erase it.
That is the terrifying shadow behind the story of Athaliah.
Most people read her story quickly. A wicked queen. A massacre. A hidden child. A dramatic overthrow.
But beneath the surface is one of the darkest spiritual wars in all of Scripture.
Because this was never just about politics.
This was a satanic attempt to stop the Messiah from ever being born.
And if you understand that... this story becomes horrifyingly personal.
Because the same spirit that tried to wipe out the royal bloodline still tries to destroy destinies today before they can mature into what God promised.
The enemy attacks what carries covenant.
And Athaliah was attacking covenant itself.
The Bible says in 2 Kings 11:1:
“When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.”
The Hebrew phrase for “royal offspring” is:
זֶרַע הַמַּמְלָכָה
Zera ha-mamlakhah
“Seed of the kingdom.”
Not merely children.
Seed.
That word matters.
Because from Genesis onward, Scripture is obsessed with the promised Seed.
Genesis 3:15 says:
“And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed...”
The Hebrew word there is also:
זֶרַע
Zera
Seed.
From the very beginning, Satan knew a coming Seed would crush his head.
So history became a war over bloodlines.
Cain kills Abel. Pharaoh murders Hebrew sons. Haman plots genocide. Herod massacres infants.
And here in Judah... Athaliah tries to annihilate the royal line of David.
Because God had made an unbreakable covenant.
In 2 Samuel 7:12–16, God promised David:
“Your throne shall be established forever.”
The Hebrew word for forever is:
עוֹלָם
Olam
An everlasting continuity. An enduring age. A covenant extending beyond human lifespan.
God promised David that the Messiah would come through his line.
Satan heard that promise.
And Athaliah became one of the enemy’s instruments to try to stop it.
But who exactly was Athaliah?
That question matters more than most people realize.
Athaliah was not simply a power-hungry queen.
She was deeply connected to one of the darkest spiritual systems in Israel’s history.
She was the daughter — or granddaughter according to some textual considerations — of Ahab and Jezebel.
That matters.
Because Jezebel’s influence was not merely immoral. It was aggressively anti-Yahweh.
The worship of Baal involved child sacrifice, sexual ritualism, occult practices, and direct rebellion against the covenant of God.
Athaliah grew up in that environment.
And when she married into Judah’s royal family, corruption entered the Davidic line through alliance.
One compromise opened the gate.
That is how darkness often enters.
Not always through invasion. Sometimes through agreement.
Second Chronicles 22 reveals how deeply destructive those alliances became.
Her son Ahaziah “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab.”
Why?
Because Athaliah counseled him.
The Bible literally says:
“His mother was his counselor to do wickedly.”
Some parents disciple children into holiness. Others disciple them into destruction.
And there are people reading this right now who are still bleeding emotionally because someone who should have protected them instead taught them darkness.
You learned rage before peace. Fear before trust. Performance before grace. Addiction before purity.
And maybe nobody sees how hard you fight internally because of what was planted in you early.
But the Gospel is powerful enough to uproot inherited darkness.
Jesus does not merely forgive sin. He breaks chains.
Athaliah understood something many believers still fail to understand:
If you can kill the next generation, you can alter the future.
That is why hell fights children.
Not because they are weak.
Because they are dangerous.
The enemy fears what they may become.
And spiritually, many people never realize they survived assassination attempts against their calling.
Some attacks were physical. Some emotional. Some sexual. Some psychological. Some spiritual.
The enemy wanted you dead before you discovered who you were in Christ.
And maybe you thought it was random.
But hell rarely attacks without purpose.
Athaliah slaughtered the royal heirs because every living descendant represented continuity of promise.
Every child was a threat to darkness.
Yet hidden inside the horror is one of the most breathtaking moments in Scripture.
One baby survives.
One.
Second Kings 11:2 says:
“But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being murdered...”
Imagine the screams. Imagine the panic. Imagine soldiers moving room to room. Imagine mothers clutching children. Imagine blood on palace floors.
And somewhere in the middle of the nightmare... God preserves one child.
Joash.
The name Joash in Hebrew is:
יוֹאָשׁ
Yoash
Meaning:
“Yahweh has given.”
That is powerful.
Because what God gives, hell cannot ultimately destroy.
Joash was hidden in the temple for six years.
Six years.
Silence. Hiddenness. Waiting.
And this is where many believers lose hope.
Because God often preserves destiny in hidden seasons.
Not every divine season looks victorious.
Some look buried. Some look forgotten. Some look delayed. Some look painfully silent.
But hidden does not mean abandoned.
The Messiah Himself would later spend years in obscurity before public ministry.
God is not intimidated by hiddenness.
Sometimes concealment is protection.
Psalm 27:5 says:
“For in the day of trouble He shall hide me in His pavilion...”
The Hebrew word for “hide” is:
יִצְפְּנֵנִי
Yitzpeneni
To treasure away. To conceal securely. To protect secretly.
God was hiding the future king while Athaliah thought she had won.
And maybe that is where some people are emotionally right now.
You feel unseen. Forgotten. Delayed. Invisible.
But what if God has been preserving you while the enemy thought he buried you?
What if your hidden season was not punishment... but protection?
Athaliah ruled for six years believing the royal line was dead.
Imagine the arrogance.
Imagine sitting on a throne you stole. Imagine believing covenant was finally broken. Imagine believing darkness had defeated prophecy.
But God had already preserved an answer inside the temple.
And one day the hidden king emerged.
Second Kings 11:12 says:
“Then he brought out the king’s son, put the crown on him, and gave him the Testimony...”
The Hebrew word for “Testimony” is:
הָעֵדוּת
Ha-edut
The covenant witness. The law. The divine testimony of God.
Notice this carefully.
The true king was revealed together with God’s covenant.
Real authority is never separated from submission to God.
Athaliah had power without covenant. Joash had covenant-backed authority.
There is a difference.
Some people have influence. Others carry anointing.
Those are not the same thing.
When Athaliah heard the celebration, she ran into the temple crying:
“Treason! Treason!”
The irony is devastating.
The usurper accused the rightful king.
Darkness often calls truth dangerous.
And we still see that today.
People mock holiness. Ridicule purity. Attack conviction. Call righteousness hateful. Call compromise wisdom.
But truth does not become false because culture hates it.
Athaliah died outside the temple.
And the covenant line survived.
Eventually that line led to Jesus Christ.
This is why the genealogy matters.
This is why Satan fought it.
Matthew opens with genealogy because Heaven was documenting covenant fulfillment.
Jesus is called:
“The Son of David.”
Not symbolically. Literally.
The royal line survived every massacre attempt.
Because God protects what He promises.
And here is the part many people need to hear deeply.
The spirit behind Athaliah still exists.
Not necessarily in a literal person.
But in systems. In ideologies. In cultural darkness. In spiritual attacks against identity, purity, covenant, and future generations.
There is still war over the seed.
There is still war over children. There is still war over families. There is still war over truth. There is still war over destiny.
The enemy still tries to kill what carries God’s future.
Some of you were targeted because of what you carry.
That depression was not random. That temptation was not random. That attack was not random. That warfare was not random.
Hell recognized purpose before you did.
And maybe that explains why your life has felt like survival for so long.
But if God preserved Joash through massacre... He can preserve you through warfare.
If God preserved the covenant line through bloodshed... He can preserve His calling on your life despite trauma, failure, addiction, betrayal, shame, or brokenness.
Some people think they are too damaged for redemption.
But the lineage of Jesus survived murder plots, prostitution, betrayal, exile, adultery, corruption, and violence.
Grace has always moved through broken history.
That is the scandalous beauty of the Gospel.
Jesus entered human history fully aware of how ugly humanity had become.
Yet He came anyway.
The Greek word used repeatedly for “save” in the New Testament is:
σῴζω
Sōzō
Not merely rescue from danger.
It means: heal, preserve, restore, make whole, deliver.
Jesus did not come merely to improve behavior.
He came to rescue what hell tried to destroy.
Including you.
There are people reading this who feel spiritually exhausted.
You smile publicly but internally feel fractured. You pray but still battle darkness. You love God but wrestle secretly. You attend church but feel numb.
And maybe you are terrified that something inside you has already died.
But Joash’s story is proof that God specializes in preserving what seems impossible to keep alive.
The covenant survived hidden.
And maybe your faith has survived hidden too.
Maybe your prayer life is weak. Maybe your heart feels tired. Maybe your fire feels small.
But small fire is still fire.
Do not let the enemy convince you that survival means failure.
Sometimes surviving is evidence that God has preserved you for a future you cannot yet see.
Athaliah tried to erase the royal line completely.
She failed.
Hell tried to stop the Messiah.
It failed.
The grave tried to hold Jesus.
It failed.
And the same Christ who overcame death is still able to sustain broken people today.
Romans 8:31 says:
“If God is for us, who can be against us?”
The Greek phrase is:
Εἰ ὁ Θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν
Ei ho Theos hyper hēmōn
“If God is on behalf of us...”
Not distant. Not passive. Not indifferent.
On behalf of us.
That changes everything.
Maybe you were attacked because Heaven marked you before hell noticed you.
Maybe your survival was not accidental.
Maybe the reason you are still here is because God preserved something the enemy could not kill.
And maybe this article found you at the exact moment you were about to give up.
Do not surrender your future to the same darkness Christ died to free you from.
Jesus is still rescuing people. Still healing people. Still restoring people. Still calling prodigals home. Still breaking chains. Still rewriting stories.
And no matter how aggressively darkness attacked your life... God still has the final word.
The enemy attacked your life because your existence threatened darkness long before you realized Heaven had marked you.
Filipino Version:
Bakit Sinubukan ni Athaliah na Lipulin Nang Tuluyan ang Maharlikang Lahi
May mga espirituwal na laban na hindi lang gustong sugatan ang isang henerasyon.
Gusto nila itong burahin.
Hindi pahinain. Hindi iligaw. Hindi lang sirain.
Burahin.
Iyan ang nakakatakot na anino sa likod ng kuwento ni Athaliah.
Madalas, mabilis lang basahin ng mga tao ang bahaging ito ng Biblia.
Isang masamang reyna. Isang patayan. Isang batang itinago. Isang pagbagsak ng trono.
Pero sa ilalim ng lahat ng iyon ay isa sa pinakamadilim na espirituwal na digmaan sa buong Kasulatan.
Dahil hindi lang ito tungkol sa politika.
Isa itong satanikong pagtatangka upang pigilan ang pagdating ng Mesiyas.
At kapag naunawaan mo iyon... magiging napakapersonal ng kuwentong ito.
Dahil ang parehong espiritu na nagtangkang wasakin ang lahi ni David ay siya ring espiritung sumusubok sirain ang mga itinakdang kapalaran ngayon bago pa man ito magbunga.
Inaatake ng kaaway ang anumang may dalang tipan.
At si Athaliah ay umatake mismo laban sa tipan ng Diyos.
Sinasabi ng 2 Hari 11:1:
“Nang makita ni Athalia na ina ni Ahazia na patay na ang kaniyang anak, siya'y tumindig at nilipol ang lahat ng maharlikang angkan.”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “maharlikang angkan” ay:
זֶרַע הַמַּמְלָכָה
Zera ha-mamlakhah
“Ibinhing pangkaharian.”
Hindi lang mga anak.
Binhi.
Mahalaga ang salitang iyon.
Dahil mula Genesis pa lamang, malinaw nang may digmaan tungkol sa ipinangakong Binhi.
Sa Genesis 3:15 sinabi ng Diyos:
“At pag-aalitin ko ikaw at ang babae, at ang iyong binhi at ang kaniyang binhi...”
Ang salitang “binhi” sa Hebreo ay:
זֶרַע
Zera
Mula pa noon, alam na ni Satanas na may darating na Binhi na dudurog sa kaniyang ulo.
Kaya naging digmaan ng mga lahi ang kasaysayan.
Pinatay ni Cain si Abel. Ipinapatay ni Faraon ang mga sanggol na Hebreo. Binalak ni Haman ang paglipol sa mga Hudyo. Pinatay ni Herodes ang mga sanggol sa Bethlehem.
At dito... sinubukan ni Athaliah na ubusin ang lahi ni David.
Dahil may ipinangako ang Diyos.
Sa 2 Samuel 7:12–16 nangako ang Panginoon kay David:
“Ang iyong trono ay matatatag magpakailanman.”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “magpakailanman” ay:
עוֹלָם
Olam
Walang hanggang pagpapatuloy. Isang tipang hindi natatapos sa kamatayan.
Nangako ang Diyos na ang Mesiyas ay manggagaling sa lahi ni David.
Narinig iyon ni Satanas.
At naging kasangkapan si Athaliah sa kaniyang tangkang pigilan ang plano ng Diyos.
Pero sino ba talaga si Athaliah?
Mas mahalaga ang tanong na iyan kaysa iniisip ng marami.
Hindi lang siya isang gahaman sa kapangyarihan.
Malalim ang koneksiyon niya sa isa sa pinakamadilim na espirituwal na sistema sa Israel.
Siya ay anak — o apo ayon sa ibang pag-aaral — nina Ahab at Jezebel.
At mahalaga iyon.
Dahil ang impluwensiya ni Jezebel ay hindi lang imoral.
Ito ay direktang laban kay Yahweh.
Kasama sa pagsamba kay Baal ang paghahandog ng mga bata, seksuwal na ritwal, okultismo, at paghihimagsik laban sa Diyos.
Doon lumaki si Athaliah.
At nang mapangasawa niya ang pamilya ni David, pumasok ang kadiliman sa loob mismo ng maharlikang linya.
Minsan, isang kompromiso lang ang kailangan upang makapasok ang pagkawasak.
Ganiyan madalas gumalaw ang kadiliman.
Hindi laging sa pamamagitan ng puwersahan.
Minsan sa pamamagitan ng kasunduan.
Sinasabi sa 2 Cronica 22 na si Ahazia ay “lumakad sa mga daan ng sambahayan ni Ahab.”
Bakit?
Dahil si Athaliah mismo ang nagturo sa kaniya.
Sinasabi ng Biblia:
“Ang kaniyang ina ang kaniyang tagapayo upang gumawa ng kasamaan.”
May mga magulang na nagtuturo ng kabanalan. May mga magulang na nagtatanim ng pagkawasak.
At may mga taong nagbabasa nito ngayon na hanggang ngayon ay sugatan pa rin dahil ang mga taong dapat sana'y nagprotekta sa kanila ay sila pang nagturo ng kadiliman.
Natuto ka ng galit bago kapayapaan. Takot bago tiwala. Pagpapanggap bago biyaya. Bisyo bago kabanalan.
At baka hindi nakikita ng iba kung gaano kalalim ang laban mo araw-araw.
Pero sapat ang kapangyarihan ni Cristo upang bunutin kahit ang mga kadilimang minana pa.
Hindi lang nagpapatawad si Jesus. Pinuputol Niya ang tanikala.
Naunawaan ni Athaliah ang bagay na hindi pa rin nauunawaan ng maraming mananampalataya ngayon.
Kapag napatay mo ang susunod na henerasyon, mababago mo ang hinaharap.
Kaya galit ang impiyerno sa mga bata.
Hindi dahil mahina sila.
Kundi dahil mapanganib sila sa kaharian ng kadiliman.
Takot ang kaaway sa maaaring maging bunga ng kanilang buhay.
At espirituwal, maraming tao ang hindi alam na nakaligtas sila sa mga tangkang pagpatay laban sa kanilang tawag.
May mga pag-atakeng pisikal. Emosyonal. Seksuwal. Mental. Espirituwal.
Gusto kang patayin ng kaaway bago mo pa malaman kung sino ka kay Cristo.
At baka akala mo noon ay malas lang.
Pero madalas may dahilan ang matinding pag-atake.
Pinatay ni Athaliah ang mga tagapagmana dahil bawat isa sa kanila ay banta sa kadiliman.
Bawat batang buhay ay patunay na hindi pa tapos ang pangako ng Diyos.
Pero sa gitna ng karumal-dumal na kuwento... may isang sanggol na nabuhay.
Isa.
Sinasabi sa 2 Hari 11:2:
“Ngunit si Jehosheba... ay kumuha kay Joas at itinago siya mula sa mga anak ng hari na pinapatay.”
Isipin mo ang sigawan. Ang takot. Ang mga sundalong naghahalughog. Ang mga inang yumayakap sa kanilang mga anak. Ang dugong nasa sahig ng palasyo.
At sa gitna ng bangungot... may itinagong isang bata ang Diyos.
Si Joas.
Sa Hebreo:
יוֹאָשׁ
Yoash
Ang ibig sabihin:
“Si Yahweh ang nagbigay.”
Napakalalim niyan.
Dahil ang ibinigay ng Diyos ay hindi kayang tuluyang sirain ng impiyerno.
Anim na taon itinago si Joas sa templo.
Anim na taon ng katahimikan. Anim na taon ng pagtatago. Anim na taon ng paghihintay.
At dito nawawalan ng pag-asa ang maraming tao.
Dahil madalas itinatago muna ng Diyos ang isang kapalaran bago Niya ito ihayag.
Hindi lahat ng banal na panahon ay mukhang matagumpay.
Minsan mukhang nakabaon. Nakalimutan. Naantala. Tahimik.
Pero hindi ibig sabihin ng pagtatago ay iniwan ka na ng Diyos.
Minsan, proteksiyon ang katahimikan.
Sinasabi sa Awit 27:5:
“Sapagkat sa araw ng kaguluhan ay ikukubli Niya ako...”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “ikukubli” ay:
יִצְפְּנֵנִי
Yitzpeneni
Ligtas na itago. Protektahan nang lihim.
Habang iniisip ni Athaliah na nanalo na siya... iniingatan na pala ng Diyos ang susunod na hari.
At baka may mga taong nakakabasa nito ngayon na ganoon din ang pakiramdam.
Pakiramdam mo hindi ka nakikita. Hindi ka napapansin. Parang nahuhuli ka sa buhay.
Pero paano kung ang pagtatago ng Diyos sa iyo ay hindi kaparusahan... kundi proteksiyon?
Anim na taon naghari si Athaliah na iniisip na tapos na ang lahi ni David.
Isipin mo ang yabang.
Akala niya natalo na niya ang tipan ng Diyos.
Pero may nakatagong sagot ang Diyos sa loob ng templo.
At dumating ang araw na inilabas ang tunay na hari.
Sinasabi sa 2 Hari 11:12:
“At inilabas nila ang anak ng hari, ipinutong ang putong sa kaniya, at ibinigay ang Patotoo...”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “Patotoo” ay:
הָעֵדוּת
Ha-edut
Ang tipan. Ang kautusan. Ang banal na patunay ng Diyos.
Pansinin mo ito.
Ang tunay na hari ay ipinakita kasama ng tipan ng Diyos.
Ang tunay na awtoridad ay hindi hiwalay sa pagsunod sa Panginoon.
May kapangyarihan si Athaliah pero walang tipan. May tipan si Joas kaya may tunay siyang awtoridad.
Magkaiba iyon.
May mga taong may impluwensiya. Pero hindi lahat ay may pahid ng Diyos.
Nang marinig ni Athaliah ang sigawan ng bayan, tumakbo siya sa templo at sumigaw:
“Pagtataksil! Pagtataksil!”
Napakalalim ng irony.
Ang tunay na taksil ang umakusa sa tunay na hari.
Ganiyan madalas ang kadiliman.
Tinatawag nitong masama ang kabanalan. Pinagtatawanan ang katotohanan. Ginagawang normal ang kasalanan.
Pero hindi nagiging kasinungalingan ang katotohanan dahil lang galit dito ang kultura.
Namatay si Athaliah.
Pero nabuhay ang tipan.
At mula sa lahing iyon dumating si Jesu-Cristo.
Kaya napakahalaga ng genealogy sa Biblia.
Kaya desperadong sirain ito ni Satanas.
Tinawag si Jesus na:
“Anak ni David.”
Hindi simboliko. Literal.
Nalampasan ng maharlikang linya ang bawat tangkang pagpatay.
Dahil pinoprotektahan ng Diyos ang Kaniyang ipinangako.
At ito ang kailangang marinig ng maraming tao ngayon.
Buhay pa rin ang espiritu sa likod ni Athaliah.
Hindi lang sa isang tao.
Kundi sa mga sistema. Sa kultura. Sa ideolohiya. Sa kadilimang umaatake sa pagkakakilanlan, pamilya, katotohanan, at susunod na henerasyon.
May digmaan pa rin laban sa binhi.
May digmaan laban sa mga bata. Sa pamilya. Sa kadalisayan. Sa katotohanan. Sa tawag ng Diyos.
At baka kaya matindi ang naging laban mo sa buhay.
Dahil may dala kang layunin.
Hindi aksidente ang pag-atake.
Maaaring nakita ng impiyerno ang potensyal mo bago mo pa nakita ang sarili mo kay Cristo.
At baka iyan ang dahilan kung bakit pakiramdam mo buong buhay mo ay puro pakikipaglaban.
Pero kung naingatan ng Diyos si Joas sa gitna ng patayan... maaari ka rin Niyang ingatan sa gitna ng iyong digmaan.
Kung naingatan Niya ang linya ng tipan sa gitna ng dugo at pagkawasak... maaari ka rin Niyang panatilihin kahit sugatan ka ng trauma, kasalanan, bisyo, pagtataksil, o kahihiyan.
Akala ng iba tapos na sila.
Pero dumaan din sa magulong kasaysayan ang lahi ni Jesus.
At kahit ganoon... dumating pa rin ang biyaya.
Iyan ang kagandahan ng Ebanghelyo.
Alam ni Jesus kung gaano kasama ang sangkatauhan.
Pero dumating pa rin Siya.
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “ligtas” sa Bagong Tipan ay:
σῴζω
Sōzō
Hindi lang iligtas mula sa panganib.
Kundi: magpagaling, magpanumbalik, magbuo muli, magligtas, mag-restore.
Hindi lang dumating si Jesus upang baguhin ang asal.
Dumating Siya upang iligtas ang mga bagay na gustong patayin ng impiyerno.
Kasama ka roon.
May mga taong nagbabasa nito na pagod na pagod na espirituwal.
Ngumingiti sa labas pero wasak sa loob. Nagsisimba pero manhid. Nanalangin pero pagod. Lumalaban pero tahimik.
At baka natatakot kang may namatay na sa loob mo.
Pero ang kuwento ni Joas ay patunay na marunong mag-ingat ang Diyos ng mga bagay na akala ng iba ay wala nang pag-asa.
Nabuhay ang tipan kahit nakatago.
At baka ganoon din ang pananampalataya mo.
Mahina. Tahimik. Pero buhay pa.
At ang maliit na apoy... apoy pa rin.
Huwag mong hayaang kumbinsihin ka ng kaaway na kabiguan ang simpleng pag-survive.
Minsan ang pag-survive ay patunay na iniingatan ka pa rin ng Diyos para sa hinaharap na hindi mo pa nakikita.
Sinubukan ni Athaliah na ubusin ang maharlikang lahi.
Nabigo siya.
Sinubukan ng impiyerno na pigilan ang Mesiyas.
Nabigo ito.
Sinubukan ng libingan na pigilan si Cristo.
Nabigo rin.
At ang parehong Jesus na nagtagumpay laban sa kamatayan ay Siya ring kayang magpanatili sa iyo ngayon.
Sinasabi sa Roma 8:31:
“If God is for us, who can be against us?”
Sa Griyego:
Εἰ ὁ Θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν
Ei ho Theos hyper hēmōn
“Kung ang Diyos ay para sa atin...”
Hindi malayo. Hindi malamig. Hindi walang pakialam.
Kundi para sa atin.
Iyan ang nagpapabago ng lahat.
Baka kaya ka inatake nang matindi dahil minarkahan ka na ng Langit bago ka pa man mapansin ng impiyerno.
Baka hindi aksidente na buhay ka pa hanggang ngayon.
Baka may iniingatan ang Diyos sa loob mo na hindi kayang patayin ng kadiliman.
At baka dumating sa iyo ang artikulong ito sa eksaktong oras na gusto mo nang sumuko.
Huwag mong isuko ang kinabukasan mo sa kadilimang matagal nang gustong sirain ka.

Si Jesus ay patuloy pa ring nagpapalaya. Patuloy pa ring nagpapagaling. Patuloy pa ring nagbabalik. Patuloy pa ring tumatawag sa mga naliligaw. Patuloy pa ring pumuputol ng tanikala. Patuloy pa ring nagsusulat muli ng mga kuwento.
At kahit gaano kalakas ang naging pag-atake laban sa buhay mo... ang Diyos pa rin ang may huling salita.
Hindi aksidente na buhay ka pa.
Inatake ka ng kadiliman dahil may nakita itong layunin sa buhay mo bago mo pa nakita ang sarili mo sa mata ng Diyos.
